Mayor Vitali Klitschko confirmed severe grid strain as emergency blackouts hit districts including Pivdenna and Borshchahivka, while drone debris struck a 25-story residential block and

Belarus Summons Ukraine Envoy Over Alleged Bryansk Drone Strike — Belarus summoned Ukraine’s chargé d’affaires on Friday, Oct. 9, accusing Ukrainian forces of deliberately striking a Belarusian commercial truck in Russia’s Bryansk region that injured a citizen. Ukrainian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi rejected the claim as groundless and provocative, protesting the summons and condemning Minsk for attempting to fabricate security threats while actively aiding Moscow’s war effort.

Allies Press Greece, Spain for Expiring Patriot Missiles — NATO and EU officials are pressing Greece and Spain to transfer Patriot PAC-2 interceptors nearing their 23-year shelf-life limit to Ukraine. With Kyiv requiring up to 360 interceptors for winter defense, and US stockpiles dipping below 1,700 due to operations in the Middle East, European allies are seeking to unlock southern European arsenals.

Latvia’s Pro-Ukraine Landslide Hides a Weakness Putin Could Exploit — Latvia’s election gave PM Kulbergs a strong mandate, but just 51.8% of eligible voters participated. For a NATO frontline state bordering Russia and Belarus, the weak turnout highlights concerns about social cohesion and the resilience of its internal defenses.
Trump’s Deal with Putin Stabs Ukraine in the Back — The US president has betrayed not only Ukraine but also Europe.

US Envoys Pressure Kyiv on Refinery Strikes — US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have warned Ukrainian negotiators in Miami that Washington could restrict intelligence sharing if Kyiv continues striking Russian oil refineries. A US official confirmed the envoys urged Kyiv not to hurt US consumers, adding that Donald Trump struck a Russian diesel deal with Vladimir Putin after President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected a unilateral strike pause without a mutual energy ceasefire.

Finland Approves 35th Military Aid Package for Ukraine — Finnish President Alexander Stubb approved the delivery of Finland’s 35th military aid package to Ukraine on Friday, Oct. 9, following an urgent appeal from Kyiv. Valued at approximately €1 million ($1.1 million), the shipment draws a single defense product from military stockpiles, bringing total Finnish defense assistance to €3.6 billion ($4 billion) as preparations begin for a broader upcoming package.

Ukraine Vows to Keep Striking Russian Refineries Despite Trump Deal – FT — Ukraine will continue long-range drone strikes on Russian oil refineries despite a commercial diesel agreement between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin, the Financial Times reported. A senior Ukrainian official pledged that Kyiv “will burn [Russian] refineries,” while analysts at Kpler noted that Russian refining operates at just 60% capacity following Ukrainian attacks, casting doubt on Moscow’s ability to fulfill export

Putin Rejects Peace Talks in Trump Call, Vows to Press War — Russian President Vladimir Putin rejected resuming peace talks and reaffirmed Moscow’s intent to press the war against Ukraine until all goals are achieved during a phone call with US President Donald Trump, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov reported. Despite Trump offering warm birthday wishes and securing a controversial sanctions waiver for Russian diesel, Putin repeated hardline demands and claimed Russian forces hold full battlefield init

Drones Strike Rostov Oil Terminal, Igniting Major Fire — Ukrainian strike drones hit the Yug Rusi oil transshipment terminal in Rostov-on-Don early Saturday morning, Oct. 10, igniting a massive blaze across the key fuel logistics facility. The terminal, which handles roughly 2.5 million metric tons of petroleum products annually from the Novoshakhtinsk refinery to supply the Russian military and export markets, was struck as regional authorities claimed over 50 drones were intercepted.

Russia Exploits School Knife Attacks for Disinformation — Polish Defense Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz announced on Friday, Oct. 9, that Russia sought to exploit two violent school knife attacks in Poland to mount a coordinated disinformation campaign and stoke public panic. While authorities found no foreign involvement in the attacks – which left one school janitor dead and 11 injured across the Mazovia region – police inspected nearly 35,000 schools and detained 59 people as cyber defens

Easing Diesel Sanctions Shows Weakness to Putin, Sybiha Says — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha warned on Friday, Oct. 9, that easing sanctions on Russian diesel will not calm global energy markets or bring peace to Ukraine, arguing that Vladimir Putin interprets such steps as Western weakness. Sybiha stated that only an energy ceasefire – which Kyiv is ready to adopt if Moscow is compelled through strength – can sustainably reduce fuel prices, criticizing Washington’s recent sanctions waiver as c

Wicker Rejects Territorial Concessions to End War in Ukraine — US Senate Armed Services Committee Chairman Roger Wicker stated in Kyiv on Friday, Oct. 9, that he cannot envision a peace settlement requiring Ukraine to surrender sovereign territory seized by Russia. The Republican senator warned that Vladimir Putin is attempting to make civilian life unbearable by targeting power, heating, and municipal water networks ahead of winter, even as separate US-led peace talks in Miami were overshadowed

Death Toll Rises to 17 in Russian Strike on Zaporizhzhia — The death toll from a Russian guided bomb attack on Zaporizhzhia rose to 17 civilians, including three children, on Saturday. The strike damaged 26 residential buildings across the Shevchenkivskyi and Voznesenivskyi districts, including a direct hit on a five-story apartment block, marking the second consecutive day of glide bomb attacks on the regional center.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 9, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 9, 2026.

Putin Touts 90% Dollar-Free CIS Trade as Russia Sidesteps Western Sanctions — At the CIS summit in Turkmenistan, Putin highlighted more than $110 billion in regional trade and 90% of settlements conducted in national currencies. While Moscow uses regional trade networks to reduce Western financial pressure, the bloc faces declining political influence. Azerbaijan will chair the CIS in 2028, while Lukashenko hopes Armenia will follow in 2029.

US Republicans Join Democrats in Warning Trump’s Russia Diesel Deal Will Hurt, Not Help — Republican Representatives Don Bacon and Michael McCaul joined Democratic Senator Richard Blumenthal in criticizing Trump’s Russian diesel agreement. Former US Ambassador Steven Pifer told Kyiv Post the deal would undermine peace efforts without significantly lowering fuel prices.

Two-Day Miami Peace Talks Wrap Up First Day, Overshadowed by Trump’s Putin Diesel Deal — US, Ukrainian and European officials met in Miami on Friday for peace talks initially planned to last two days. The discussions were overshadowed by Trump’s surprise diesel agreement with Putin. No breakthrough was announced, and Witkoff did not confirm whether talks would resume Saturday.

Russian Guided Bombs Strike 5-Story Residential Building in Zaporizhzhia – People Feared Trapped — Russian forces struck Zaporizhzhia with guided aerial bombs early Saturday, Oct. 10, hitting a five-story residential building. Regional officials warned that people could be trapped beneath the rubble as emergency crews responded.

Trump Names Truth Social Adviser Katie Zacharia as New White House Press Secretary — US President Donald Trump has selected Katie Zacharia, a senior communications adviser at Truth Social, as the new White House press secretary. Zacharia previously served as a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson and worked on Trump’s presidential campaigns.

Ex-US Ambassador: Trump’s Russian Diesel Deal Won’t Lower Prices but Will Undermine Peace — In an exclusive Kyiv Post interview, former US Ambassador to Ukraine Steven Pifer called Donald Trump’s decision to ease Russian diesel sanctions “very unwise,” warning it would help finance Moscow’s war, undermine peace negotiations and have little impact on US fuel prices.

Kyiv Urges Graham Sanctions as Trump Cuts Deal With Putin — Zelensky urged a bipartisan US congressional delegation visiting Kyiv to enforce the Lindsey Graham sanctions law and accelerate joint Patriot interceptor production. The meeting took place under a Russian drone threat, as Trump struck a diesel deal with Putin that could provide Moscow with fresh revenue to sustain its invasion.

Zelensky: Ukrainian Peace Team in Florida Used as ‘Smokescreen’ for US-Russia Diesel Deal — President Zelensky delivered a blistering rebuke of Washington for easing sanctions on Russian diesel while Ukrainian officials negotiated peace in Florida, warning that Donald Trump was handing Vladimir Putin fresh resources to prolong the war.

Russian Drones Threaten Kyiv and Multiple Ukrainian Regions in Early Hours of Saturday — Russian forces continued launching drones across Ukraine in the early hours of Saturday, Oct. 10, triggering air raid alerts in Kyiv and other regions.

Trump Says He and Putin Have Cut Diesel Deal, Zelensky Accuses Washington of ‘Weakness’ — US President Donald Trump announced that Russia would supply diesel to global markets. Shortly after, the US Treasury Department authorized the sale and import of Russian diesel fuel through April 7, 2027. President Volodymyr Zelensky called it an “obvious weakness.”

Ukraine's Inflation Jumps to 10% as Prices Post Sharpest Monthly Spike This Year — Ukraine's annual inflation accelerated to 10.0% in September from 8.1% in August, as consumer prices rose 2.1% month-on-month, the State Statistics Service reported. Core inflation climbed to 8.8% from 8.1%, breaking a three-month plateau, while food, education and transport costs all accelerated sharply.

Russia Strikes Dnipropetrovsk Region Nearly 40 Times, Killing 1 and Setting Warehouses Ablaze — Russia struck the Dnipropetrovsk region with drones, artillery and missiles nearly 40 times on Friday, Oct. 9, killing one person. According to the head of the Dnipropetrovsk Regional Military Administration, Oleksandr Hanzha, Russia struck a logistics company’s warehouses in Dnipro district twice during the evening, causing fires.

Ukrainian Drone Tech Firms Launch Thermal Sensor Project in Europe and US — The Fourth Law and Odd Systems have unveiled Project Foundation, an initiative to mass-produce uncooled thermal sensors in Europe and the US from 2027. The companies say the project aims to quadruple European output and double US output within three years. Headquartered in Eindhoven, it plans to use partner production lines and dedicated facilities, although financing details have not been disclosed.

Sybiha Presses WTO Chief on Black Sea Shipping, Remote Audits — Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha spoke with World Trade Organization (WTO) chief Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala to back efforts on restoring Black Sea shipping safety, as Russian attacks on civilian vessels and ports threaten Ukraine’s grain exports and global food security. Sybiha also sought support for a WTO standard on remote audits.

US Congress Delegation Backs Expanded Starlink Access for Ukraine — A US congressional delegation visiting Kyiv on Friday, Oct. 9 backed efforts to persuade Elon Musk to expand Ukraine’s Starlink access, Ukrinform reported. The remarks came as Kyiv seeks to use the satellite network for drone strikes on Russian missile launchers – a request US President Donald Trump reportedly declined to support.

US Sanctions International Criminal Court; Rubio: ‘Either the ICC Will End Its Threats, or We Will End the ICC’ — The Trump administration sanctioned the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday, Oct. 9, potentially barring US companies from serving it. The move, announced only hours after a former ICC judge won the Nobel Peace Prize, escalates a previous US campaign against the court over its Israel and Afghanistan probes.

Endeavor Catalyst Backs 3 Ukrainian Tech Firms in $320M Funding — Three Ukrainian-rooted companies, Preply, Headway Inc. and HOLYWATER TECH, are backed by Endeavor Catalyst, which closed its oversubscribed Fund V at $320 million. Assets under management now exceed $850 million. Preply, Headway Inc.

Witkoff, Kushner Pitch ‘New Ideas’ to Ukraine in Miami — US presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will present Ukrainian and European officials with “new ideas” aimed at breaking the diplomatic deadlock over Russia’s war. The Friday meeting in Miami could be followed by another trip to Moscow later this month.

Planning to return to Ukraine now or in the future? The “Dodomu” platform can help you prepare — Many Ukrainians abroad are weighing a return, now or after the war ends, but the answers they need are spread across dozens of websites. The “Dodomu” platform brings them together: users can build a personalised return plan, explore profiles of 149 communities, and find Unity Hubs abroad for consultations. Launched in June 2026, the pilot has recorded over 50,000 visits and invites users to share fee

Medvedev Warns Against Travel to Europe, Claims It Is ‘Targeting Russians’ — Russian Security Council Deputy Chairman Dmitry Medvedev urged Russians to avoid European countries, claiming they risk arrest in a campaign targeting Russian citizens. His comments followed the detention of Rybar founder Mikhail Zvinchuk, his wife and three others in Montenegro. Medvedev also suggested expanding Russia’s pool of European and American detainees to exchange for Russians held abroad.

Russian Refinery Seeks Air Defense Operators Amid Escalating Drone Strikes — On Friday, the Kuibyshev Oil Refinery in Russia's Samara region advertised for operators of “Shilka” anti-aircraft guns and “Berezhok” armored vehicles to help defend the facility against Ukrainian drone strikes. According to reports, successful applicants would join Russia's mobilization reserve, undergo additional training, and serve in crews tasked with protecting the refinery and other strategic facilities from aeri

14-Year-Old Girl Accused of Poisoning, Strangling Ukrainian Soldier on Russian Handler’s Video Call — A 14-year-old girl in Rivne is accused of poisoning and strangling a Ukrainian soldier under instructions from a Russian handler. A separate case involving the alleged arson of a military vehicle has also reached court.

Ukraine’s Ground Robots Rescued 45 Soldiers Under Fire, Commander Says — Ground robots operated by Ukraine’s Artan intelligence unit evacuated 45 Ukrainian soldiers from under enemy fire during the summer campaign. The platforms traversed a combined 4,258 kilometers (2,646 miles), delivered more than 41 tons of supplies and transported captured Russian troops. Zelensky previously set a target to procure 50,000 ground drones for the military in 2026.

Zelensky Criticizes Kyiv Authorities as Russian Strikes Damage Ukraine’s Power Grid — President Volodymyr Zelensky criticized Kyiv authorities over delayed resilience measures as Russian strikes damaged Ukraine’s power grid. He said repairs were proceeding around the clock and called for additional energy equipment and air defenses. Mayor Vitali Klitschko has defended the capital’s preparations, warning that limited resources and continued attacks threaten essential services. Zelensky also repor

Russia Seizes 25 Civilians, Including Children, From Kharkiv Region, Ombudsman Says — Russian forces forcibly removed 25 civilians, including children, from an occupied part of the Kharkiv region and took them to an unknown location, Ukraine’s ombudsman said. Dmytro Lubinets accused Moscow of presenting coercive transfers as evacuations and collecting residents’ personal information. He demanded disclosure of the civilians’ whereabouts and conditions, called for their return and appealed to inte

Montenegro Detains Russian Z-Blogger Targeted by US — Montenegrin authorities reportedly detained Zvinchuk, his wife, and three others on Friday, Oct. 9. Local media reported a national security investigation, while Rybar said its team was in Montenegro legally to film a documentary.

How Real is the Threat of War in Europe? — European officials and media warn of rising Russian threats, including hybrid attacks, sabotage, disinformation, and potential military aggression against NATO countries. Commentators argue that Moscow seeks to exploit European fears of war, weaken support for Ukraine, and test Europe’s defences. Concerns are growing over missile and drone capabilities, border provocations, and possible Russian escalation ahead of US midterm elections.

Ukrainian Drone Strike Disables Several Modules at Yandex Data Center in Kaluga, Company Says — Ukrainian drones struck Yandex data centers in Russia’s Ryazan and Kaluga oblasts on Oct. 8 and 9, disabling equipment and disrupting online services used by Russian companies, including Russian Railways and telecom operator MegaFon.

African Nations Seek Return of Citizens Captured Fighting for Russia in Ukraine — Kenya and Botswana are seeking the return of citizens held in Ukraine, saying some were promised civilian jobs before being forced to serve in Russia’s military. Ukraine estimates that at least 1,700 African nationals have fought for Russia, while some captured by Kyiv have previously told Kyiv Post they were sent to the front under false pretenses.

Russia Lifts Quarantine as WHO Seeks Plague Answers — Authorities in Russia’s Irkutsk region lifted quarantine measures imposed after the unexplained death of a 28-year-old employee of an anti-plague institute. Officials say testing found no dangerous pathogens, while the WHO says it still lacks the full picture and has requested further information from Moscow.

Russia Steps Up Production of Improved Su-34 ‘Fullback’ Bombers — Russia’s Aerospace Forces received an unspecified number of Su-34 fighter bombers on Wednesday, Oct. 7 – the second such delivery in 2026. The CEO of Russia’s United Aircraft Corporation (UAC) said the production of the upgraded variation of the aircraft would continue at accelerated rates. The company is said to have delivered 18 airframes spreaded through seven batches in 2025 despite foreign sanctions.

South Africa’s Navi Pillay Wins Nobel Peace Prize — South African jurist Navi Pillay, who led the Rwanda genocide tribunal and headed a UN commission that accused Israel of genocide in Gaza, has been awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. The committee praised her efforts to prosecute war crimes and defend international law amid mounting pressure on global justice institutions.

Ukraine Strikes Russian Missile Fuel Plant, Oil Depot, Yandex Data Center as Moscow Claims 505 Drones Downed — Ukrainian drones struck a Russian chemical plant producing cruise missile fuel, damaged a Yandex data center in Kaluga for the second consecutive day and reportedly sparked a fire at an oil depot near Belgorod. Moscow claimed its air defenses downed 505 Ukrainian drones overnight.

Austria Releases Ukrainian Investigative Journalist Mykhailo Tkach After Detention in Vienna — Austrian police detained Ukrainian investigative journalist Mykhailo Tkach and cameraman Yaroslav Bondarenko in Vienna while on assignment. Ukrainska Pravda, their employer, demanded their release. Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry sought explanations and consular access, but no charges were announced.

Klitschko Warns Kyiv Faces a Fight for Survival as Russian Strikes Threaten Winter Preparations — Kyiv Mayor Klitschko warned that intensified Russian strikes on bridges and energy infrastructure are threatening the capital’s preparations for winter. He urged residents with family outside the city to consider temporarily relocating as authorities prepare backup heating and supplies.

Trump May Leave 100,000 Ukrainians in US Immigration Limbo Rather Than Renew Protections — The Trump administration faces an Oct. 19 deadline to decide the fate of temporary protected status for more than 100,000 Ukrainians in the US. Lawmakers are weighing a possible 6-month extension through inaction, though it could leave recipients in legal limbo.

US, Ukrainian Delegations to Discuss Peace in Miami as Trump’s Envoys May Return to Moscow — US and Ukrainian delegations will meet in Miami to discuss new peace proposals, including a possible ceasefire covering energy infrastructure and grain shipments. US envoys Witkoff and Kushner may travel to Moscow later this month for further talks with Putin.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 8, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 8, 2026.

German Spy Scandal – Could Ukraine and NATO Be at Risk? — The arrest of former German intelligence chief August Hanning over nearly 2,000 classified documents has exposed alleged Azerbaijani intelligence links and renewed scrutiny of his seven trips to Russia. Baku’s  intelligence cooperation with Moscow and secret German-Russian meetings in Azerbaijan raise questions about potential risks to Ukraine and NATO allies, although no Russian role in the alleged espionage has been established.

Ukrainian Child Rescue Advocate Among Nobel Peace Prize Contenders as Trump Eyes Award — The 2026 Nobel Peace Prize will be announced in Oslo on Friday, Oct. 9, with Ukrainian child rescue advocate Mykola Kuleba among the potential contenders identified by experts. US President Donald Trump has openly sought the award, although Nobel observers consider his chances slim. Humanitarian organizations, press freedom advocates and international justice institutions are also being discussed.

Russian Strike Near Apartment Building in Zaporizhzhia Kills 1, Injures 7 — One man was killed and 7 people wounded after a Russian strike near a high-rise residential building in Zaporizhzhia early Friday, Oct. 9.

Putin, Pezeshkian Talk ‘Peace’ in Turkmenistan While Fueling War in Ukraine — Putin and Pezeshkian reaffirmed their strategic partnership during an Oct. 8 meeting in Turkmenistan. Putin pledged support for Tehran, while Pezeshkian criticized US foreign policy and discussed revised peace proposals.

Russia Launches Fresh Wave of Deadly Attacks Across Ukraine – Kyiv Under Drone Threat — Russia launched another overnight assault Friday, Oct. 9, killing a man in Zaporizhzhia and threatening Kyiv with jet-powered drones. Regional authorities reported fresh injuries as Russian guided-bomb and drone attacks continued.

Russian Drone Attack Kills Civilian in Western Ukraine’s Ivano-Frankivsk — A Russian drone attack on Ivano-Frankivsk late Thursday killed a 67-year-old civilian. Regional authorities reported falling drone debris and a fire, while the city’s mayor confirmed the victim was a security guard.

Budanov Heads to US With Ukrainian Negotiating Team for ‘Important Meetings,’ European Leaders Set to Join — Head of the Presidential Office Kyrylo Budanov confirmed on Thursday, Oct. 8 that he was traveling to the US with Ukraine’s negotiating team for “important meetings.” The delegation is scheduled to meet with senior US special envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, who stepped up their efforts to broker an end to Russia’s war in recent months. According to President Volodymyr Zelensky, an

Zelensky Says Ukraine Is Aware of US-Russia Economic Discussions — President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Thursday, Oct. 8, that Kyiv is aware about various US-Russia dialogues but is not ready to discuss them publicly. Although it was not specified which discussions he was referring to, his remarks followed an earlier report on Thursday that claimed Jared Kushner and Kirill Dmitriev discussed bringing an American investor into Nord Stream.

UK Announces $71M Winter Aid, New Sanctions on Russia — UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband announced £54 million ($71 million) in winter energy and humanitarian aid for Ukraine, while also revealing around 40 new sanctions on Russia during his first visit to Ukraine as foreign secretary on Thursday, Oct. 8. Together with President Volodymyr Zelensky and Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, he visited Pryluky, a city in the Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile killed 22 people on Wednesday.
A “Muslim NATO” Just Activated Its Own Article 5 — For the first time in history, an Article 5-style collective defense agreement has been activated outside of NATO.

Zelensky Visits Pryluky With UK’s Miliband, Thanks EU for €1.2B Tranche for Drones — President Volodymyr Zelensky visited Pryluky with UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband on Thursday, Oct. 8, after a Russian barrage left 22 civilians dead, including five children. The president ordered housing aid and shelter inspections, while separately thanking the EU for a €1.2 billion ($1.4 billion) tranche that Kyiv aims to spend on air defense, particularly drones, ahead of winter.

Trump Envoys in Talks With Putin’s Money Man Over Russian Gas, Reports Say — Senior US envoy Jared Kushner and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev have reportedly discussed bringing a US investor into the Nord Stream gas pipelines, five sources familiar with the matter told Reuters on Thursday, Oct. 8. The pipelines remain under both US and EU sanctions due to Russia’s war in Ukraine, and Germany strongly opposes reopening them.

Ukraine’s Spec Ops Hit Omsk Oil Refinery 2,500 km Away – Again — Ukraine’s SSO says it struck the Omsk Oil Refinery for the second time, with drones traveling nearly 3,000 km (1,864 miles). Russian outlet Astra reported a fire and growing queues at gas stations in Omsk, with the last attack recorded in July.

Trump ‘Can And Should’ Do More: Zelensky Slams US-Russia Business Talks — Ukrainian negotiators will visit the United States on Oct. 9–10, President Volodymyr Zelensky said during a visit to Pryluky following a deadly Russian strike. He urged Donald Trump to increase pressure on Moscow and criticized discussions of future economic cooperation with Russia.

How to Build a Business Despite the War and Where to Find the Strength: Takeaways From the Fourth Forbes Ukraine CEO Summit — Ukrainian business leaders at the fourth Forbes Ukraine CEO Summit in Kyiv shared strategies for sustaining companies, teams and themselves through the war, from decentralizing operations to supporting employee wellbeing and building resilient organizations.

Russian Attack Warehouses of Auchan, Paper Mill, Publisher, Auto Shop — Russian forces launched a massive assault on Ukrainian civilian businesses overnight on Oct. 6-7, severely damaging multiple civilian commercial storage hubs. The targeted facilities included warehouses operated by the Auchan retail chain, Knygolove publisher, ATL auto services, and a paper mill.

Ukraine Codifies 310-km/h Drone Interceptor as Kyiv Expands Its Counter-Drone Arsenal — Ukraine’s Defense Ministry has codified the Blade interceptor, clearing it for procurement and military use. Developed by Phantom Defense, the drone can reach 310 km/h, operate within 30 kilometers and carry a payload of up to 0.5 kilograms.

Pentagon Adds 1,320 Ukrainian F10 Drones to Drone Dominance Order — The US military ordered another 1,320 F10 strike drones from Ukraine's F-Drones under the Drone Dominance program, the company told Militarnyi. The batch is due by the end of November, but depends entirely on a new Ukrainian export permit.

‘Thousands Ready This Year’: Ukraine to Get SPYS Interceptors — Quantum Systems says a letter of intent has been signed for tens of thousands of SPYS drone interceptors for Ukraine, with Germany financing the program. Thousands could be delivered this year, while production may reach several thousand units per month.

Lithuania Deploys Troops to Kaliningrad Border — The Lithuanian Defense Minister responded to a request by the Interior Minister to bolster the border with Kaliningrad by deploying around 100 troops to support border guards. The move came after concerns were raised by an incursion by illegal immigrants across the Latvia-Belarus border overnight on Oct. 5-6.

Shadow Tanker Hit by Ukrainian Drones Threatens Spill Off Russia's Black Sea Coast — A Ukrainian drone strike set the 107,000-ton Aframax Rio ablaze 30 km (15 nautical miles) off Sochi. Russian officials say no pollution occurred and reopened beaches, while reports indicate oil spilled and burned on the water.

Leaked Russian Blueprint Counts 1,000 Weapons to Freeze Ukraine — An alleged Russian analytical document obtained by Schemes calculates that Moscow would need about 1,000 drones, bombs and ballistic missiles to disable 60 critical Ukrainian facilities. Kyiv, Kharkiv and Odesa are identified as the principal targets, although experts caution that the document is a weapons-requirement estimate rather than a final operational order.

Kyiv's Water Supply Disrupted After Russia's Energy Grid Strike — Kyiv authorities reported water supply disruptions on Thursday as Russian attacks on the energy grid affected water pumps across the city, with extensive blackouts also reported months ahead of winter. With Russia’s energy campaign beginning in earnest in late September and extensive blackouts already seen in Kyiv, concerns are growing over what awaits the city this winter.

4 Killed, 19 Injured as Russian Drones Assault Kyiv in Fresh Attacks — Russian drone attacks killed four people and injured 19 in Kyiv on Thursday, with a UAV hitting a four-story store in the Solomianskyi district. The attacks came a day after Russian weapons killed at least four people in the capital.

Poland Ends Russian Drone Probe After Failing to Identify Perpetrator — Polish prosecutors closed an investigation into the 2025 Russian drone incursion after failing to identify who directed it. More than 30 drones entered Polish airspace, some carried Polish SIM cards, and prosecutors found the military’s response followed procedures.

Russia Kills 30 in Kramatorsk Bus Strike as Donetsk Orders Public Transport Halt — A Russian strike on a passenger bus in Kramatorsk killed 30 people and wounded 18, according to Donetsk authorities. In response, public transport was suspended in Kramatorsk and Sloviansk as officials urged residents to evacuate.

South Korea Recalls Ambassador From Ukraine Amid Diplomatic Rift Over North Korean POWs — South Korea is recalling its ambassador from Ukraine amid a diplomatic dispute over Kyiv’s disclosure of two North Korean prisoners of war transferred to Seoul. The move follows weeks of tensions over the transfer and comes as Seoul faces scrutiny over fuel shipments to Russia.

WATCH: Downed Russian Jet Drone Crashes Near Kyiv Cars — Dramatic footage published by a local Telegram channel appears to show a downed Russian jet-powered drone falling beside cars in Kyiv. Officials have not confirmed the precise location or reported whether the incident caused casualties.

Russia Is Targeting Kyiv’s Bridges: How Resilient Are They? — Russia is attacking bridges in Kyiv, causing significant traffic jams. City authorities are considering various options for solving transportation problems, while many are asking a big question – can Kyiv’s bridges withstand regular enemy attacks?

Russia Steps Up Sabotage Attacks on Danish Defense Firms, Intelligence Says — Russia has stepped up sabotage operations targeting Danish defense companies supplying Ukraine, using increasingly bold recruits to disrupt weapons production, Denmark’s intelligence service said. Copenhagen warned the activity marks an escalation in Moscow’s hybrid warfare campaign against Western support for Kyiv.

South Korea Says Alleged Russia Fuel Shipments Not Banned — South Korea said alleged shipments of diesel to Russia did not violate its export controls, while stressing that the fuel’s origin remains under investigation. The dispute has further strained Seoul-Kyiv ties amid tensions over Ukraine’s handling of captured North Korean soldiers.

Ukraine Strikes Yandex Data Center, Russian Oil Refinery Overnight — Ukraine struck a Yandex data center in Russia’s Ryazan Oblast. Yandex is one of Russia’s largest technology companies and the country’s dominant search engine, offering services including cloud computing, online storage, email, maps and ride-hailing. Ukraine also struck a major oil refinery in Bashkortostan.

Ukraine Opens Gas Exports for Private Producers for First Time Since 2022 — The Cabinet of Ministers on Oct. 7 approved partial exports of domestically produced gas, letting private producers sell up to 15% of the previous month's output abroad through exchange auctions. The decision follows a gas surplus in the commercial segment, a wide gap between Ukrainian and European prices, and storage levels above the government's target.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, November 7, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on November 7, 2026.

Lithuania Approves €15M ($16.8M) for Ukraine’s Recovery and Reconstruction Through World Bank, EIB — Lithuania approved €15 million ($16.8 million) for Ukraine’s recovery, allocating €10 million ($11.2 million) through the World Bank’s SPUR 2.0 program and €5 million ($5.6 million) through the EIB’s EU4U Fund. Finance Minister Taurimas Valys pledged continued support for Ukraine’s victory and reconstruction.

New Russian Drone Wave Targets Kyiv and Western Ukraine After Deadly Strikes on Putin’s Birthday — Russian jet-powered drones threatened Kyiv, Lutsk and other Ukrainian cities in the early hours of Thursday, Oct. 8. The renewed alerts followed a devastating day of Russian attacks that killed at least 28 people, including five children, and damaged residential buildings across Ukraine.

Bipartisan US Senators Press Trump Administration to Crack Down on Russia’s Shadow Fleet Ahead of Oct. 18 Deadline — Democratic Senator Jeanne Shaheen and Republican Senator Roger Wicker urged Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to use new sanctions powers against Russia’s shadow fleet, illicit financial networks and military technology suppliers ahead of the Oct. 18 implementation deadline.

Russian Opposition Condemns EU Decision to Lift Usmanov Sanctions Without Freeing Political Prisoners — Russian opposition figures criticized France for securing the removal of Kremlin-linked billionaire Alisher Usmanov from EU sanctions in connection with the release of a French prisoner in Azerbaijan. They warned that the decision weakened Europe’s sanctions policy and failed to secure the release of Russian political prisoners. The deal also drew criticism in Azerbaijan.
